pl-l2d41c2-d1e105.summary: Explains that good is taken in many ways, as useful, rewardable, sign of good, appearance of good, licit, and others; only intention directed by faith is rewardable for life, but not only it is good; if a Jew or bad Christian relieves a neighbor's need led by natural piety, he does good with a good will.
claims: Natural piety can produce good acts without merit for life.

pl-l2d41c2.summary: Explains, on that view, that 'good' has many senses: useful, rewardable, sign of good, appearance of good, licit, and perhaps others. Only intention directed by faith is rewardable for life, but not only it is good: a Jew or bad Christian who relieves a neighbor's need from natural piety does good, with a good will.
claims: 'Good' is said in many ways: useful, rewardable, sign of good, appearance of good, licit.
Only intention directed by faith is rewardable for eternal life.
Acts from natural piety without faith can be good.
